subtopicTitle: Gravity assist (slingshot) — patched conic, v-infinity vectors

cards.front: Define $v_\infty$ (hyperbolic excess velocity) for a spacecraft approaching a planet.
cards.back: $v_\infty$ is the asymptotic speed of the spacecraft relative to the planet as $r\to\infty$ on the incoming or outgoing hyperbola. In the planet-centered frame, $|\vec{v}_\text{sc}-\vec{v}_\text{planet}|\to v_\infty$ far from the planet.

cards.front: What is the patched-conic approximation used for gravity-assist trajectories?
cards.back: The solar-system trajectory is divided into successive two-body conic arcs: heliocentric ellipse/hyperbola between planets, then planetocentric hyperbola during each flyby, with instantaneous sphere-of-influence switches.

cards.front: In the planet frame, why does a gravity assist leave $v_\infty$ magnitude unchanged but rotate its direction?
cards.back: Gravity is a conservative central force; specific energy $\frac12v_\infty^2$ is constant along the hyperbola. The trajectory is symmetric about the periapsis vector, producing a pure rotation of $\vec{v}_\infty^\text{in}$ into $\vec{v}_\infty^\text{out}$ by deflection angle $\delta$.

cards.front: Write the vector relation linking heliocentric velocity before and after a flyby.
cards.back: $\vec{v}_\text{helio}^\text{out}=\vec{v}_\text{planet}+\vec{v}_\infty^\text{out}$, where $\vec{v}_\infty^\text{out}$ is $\vec{v}_\infty^\text{in}$ rotated by $\delta$ about the planet's pole. The planet velocity itself is unchanged.

cards.front: Give the exact expression for the hyperbolic deflection angle $\delta$ as a function of eccentricity $e$.
cards.back: $\delta=2\arcsin(1/e)$ or equivalently $\delta=2\arccos(-1/e)$, where $e=1+(r_p v_\infty^2/\mu)$ and $r_p$ is periapsis radius.

cards.front: Derive the maximum possible speed gain $\Delta v_\text{helio}$ from a gravity assist (ideal 180° turn).
cards.back: Maximum rotation of $\vec{v}_\infty$ is 180°, so $\Delta\vec{v}_\text{helio}=2v_\infty$ in the direction of planet motion. Thus $\Delta v_\text{helio,max}=2v_\infty$ when the flyby is exactly retrograde relative to the planet's velocity vector.

cards.front: Under what condition does a gravity assist increase rather than decrease heliocentric orbital energy?
cards.back: Energy increases when the angle between $\vec{v}_\text{planet}$ and $\vec{v}_\infty^\text{out}$ is smaller than between $\vec{v}_\text{planet}$ and $\vec{v}_\infty^\text{in}$ (i.e., the spacecraft's velocity component in the planet's direction grows). This occurs for prograde flybys with turning that aligns $\vec{v}_\infty^\text{out}$ closer to $\vec{v}_\text{planet}$.
